children: , rose 4.4% to $91.27 at 10:58 a.m. ET Tuesday as Truist maintained its Buy rating and $165 price target. The analyst's case rests on pricing power, citing a calculated cumulative increase of 37.5%. That target puts potential upside at 80.8% from Tuesday's quoted price. The opportunity is big. So is the execution burden.

CoreWeave reported approximately $40 million in annualized revenue per megawatt from recent three-to-six-month contracts. It also secured more than $25 billion in customer commitments early in the third quarter and increased contracted power to 4.2 gigawatts from 3.7 gigawatts. Those commitments were additional to its $104 billion backlog at the end of June. Demand keeps piling up. Turning it into delivered computing capacity is the next test.

The GF Score of just 8/100 highlights weak overall fundamentals despite the upbeat pricing story. Second-quarter net interest expense reached $640 million, equivalent to 24.9% of revenue of $2.575 billion. That is a heavy financing load. Better contract pricing helps, but the investment case needs capacity deliveries to generate operating income fast enough to keep pace with debt costs.

title: CoreWeave Stocks Jump 4.4% Although Pricing Power Faces a $640 Million Interest Test
